By analyzing sets of related prior works that inspired human research papers, the study prompts LLMs to generate new ideas and profiles these ideas using a two-axis taxonomy based on opportunity patterns and research paradigms. The findings reveal a consistent gap: LLM-generated ideas tend to cluster around bridge-like opportunities and synthesis methods, while human ideas are more broadly distributed across different ways of framing research gaps and contributions. This research highlights that although advanced LLMs can produce a variety of reasonable research ideas, their range is narrower and systematically different from human research preferences. The study provides a nuanced understanding of the differences in ideation between humans and LLMs, suggesting that current models may have limitations in capturing the full diversity of human research creativity.

entry.title: Researchers propose a multi-objective framework to automatically optimize prompts for LLM-based user simulators in conversational recommender systems, improving behavioral alignment and addressing bias and data issues [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
entry.summary: Researchers have developed a multi-objective framework to automatically optimize prompts for large language model (LLM)-based user simulators in conversational recommender systems (CRSs). This approach aims to improve the alignment of simulated user behavior with real human interactions while addressing challenges such as systematic bias, data leakage, and limited behavioral diversity that affect current methods. The framework reduces reliance on manual prompt engineering, which typically requires extensive domain expertise. Conversational recommender systems enable dynamic user engagement by eliciting preferences and adapting recommendations in real time, but evaluating these systems through human studies is costly and time-consuming. Additionally, privacy concerns limit access to real interaction data for training. By generating synthetic user interactions, LLM-based simulators offer a promising solution, and the proposed framework enhances their effectiveness by optimizing prompts automatically. Experimental results show that this method outperforms baseline approaches across various prompt settings, advancing the development and evaluation of CRSs.

entry.title: Researchers propose Profile-guided Personalized Retrieval Optimization to improve user-aware memory retrieval in long-term conversational agents, showing gains on LoCoMo and LongMemEval-S benchmarks [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
entry.summary: Researchers have introduced Profile-guided Personalized Retrieval Optimization (PPRO), a new framework designed to enhance memory retrieval in long-term conversational agents by making it user-aware and optimizable. PPRO constructs episodic and semantic memory banks from dialogue histories and creates a user profile that guides memory ranking, accounting for individual user attributes and preferences. This approach improves the relevance of recalled information for each user, addressing limitations in existing systems that rely mainly on query similarity or fixed ranking rules. PPRO also incorporates a query rewriter trained with Group Relative Policy Optimization, which uses feedback from both retrieval quality and downstream answer accuracy while keeping memory banks and answer models fixed. Experiments on the LoCoMo and LongMemEval-S benchmarks demonstrate consistent performance improvements over both training-free and training-based memory retrieval methods. Ablation studies confirm that both profile-guided ranking and retrieval-oriented rewriting significantly contribute to these gains, highlighting the importance of retrieval optimization in personalized long-term memory for conversational agents.

entry.title: Researchers characterize destination-labeled self-looping systems with dwell, establish realization cost as sum of dwell values, and provide recognition algorithm for finite-state symbolic controllers
entry.summary: Researchers have developed a model called destination-labeled self-looping systems with dwell (DLSL systems) to study finite-state symbolic controllers where visible transitions are predetermined and each state has a minimum dwell time. They identified that imposing dwell requirements complicates departure decisions and characterized the deterministic transducers that can realize these systems as fiber-linear graph-respecting transducers. The study establishes that enforcing dwell values requires a number of control states equal to the sum of the dwell times and provides an efficient recognition and reconstruction algorithm for these systems. The research further demonstrates that under certain assumptions, equivalent realizations over the same visible graph are isomorphic, meaning the visible transduction uniquely determines the dwell vector and local decision maps. Additionally, the analysis extends to a variant where transitions can enter intermediate phases of successor fibers, broadening the applicability of the model.

entry.title: Researchers present CogTax, a four-level cognitive taxonomy integrating cognitive complexity and operational impact for command-line computing education, achieving 89% accuracy in automatic classification of Linux/bash commands [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
entry.summary: Researchers have developed CogTax, a four-level cognitive taxonomy designed to enhance command-line computing education by integrating cognitive complexity with the operational impact of commands. This taxonomy addresses a critical gap in existing educational frameworks by considering both the mental processes involved and the real-world consequences of command execution, ranging from safe read-only operations to advanced system management tasks. CogTax provides educators with a structured approach to course design and assessment, while offering students a clear framework for self-evaluation and identifying learning gaps. To enable scalable application without requiring manual expert annotation, the team trained a classifier combining syntactic features from abstract syntax trees with semantic embeddings. Tested on 585 expert-labeled Linux/bash commands, this method achieved an 89% accuracy rate, outperforming models using either representation alone. The approach also shows promise for cross-language adaptability due to structural similarities across command languages.

entry.title: Researchers find memory architecture influences language emergence in LLM agents more than channel capacity, with persistent notebooks enabling stable coordination in signaling games [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
entry.summary: Researchers investigated how two agents develop a shared language from scratch in a Lewis signaling game, focusing on the impact of memory architecture versus channel capacity in large language model (LLM) agents. They found that memory architecture plays a more crucial role than channel capacity in enabling stable coordination. Specifically, agents equipped with a persistent private notebook achieved the most reliable coordination by externalizing learned conventions, which prevented the collapse seen in stateless agents as vocabulary size increased. The study tested five different memory architectures across various channel capacities and observed that stateless agents performed best at moderate capacity but declined as the vocabulary grew beyond what their limited context window could track. Contrary to predictions based on an information bottleneck theory, surplus channel capacity generally improved coordination rather than an optimal capacity matching the number of objects. The findings highlight that both memory architecture and channel capacity are essential to understanding how agents transform interaction history into stable language conventions.

entry.title: Researchers develop an LLM-based framework for intent-driven network topology design, evaluating structural validity and resilience across four realistic scenarios with public dataset benchmarks [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
entry.summary: Researchers have developed a framework that uses Large Language Models (LLMs) to design network topologies based on natural language requirements. This approach combines hierarchical modeling with systematic validation to ensure the generated topologies are structurally valid and meet specified constraints. The framework was tested across four realistic network scenarios using both proprietary and open-weight LLMs, with results benchmarked against public datasets. The evaluation measured structural accuracy through node and edge F1-scores compared to reference topologies and assessed network resilience using server and content connectivity metrics. The study also identified common failure modes such as interface mismatches and directional inconsistencies in the generated designs. This work offers a comprehensive benchmark for understanding how LLMs handle structural and resilience constraints in network topology synthesis, aiding in informed model selection for AI-driven network design.

entry.title: Researchers introduce Rosetta, a composable native multimodal pretraining framework using Momentum-Anchored Orthogonal Projection to prevent catastrophic forgetting and enable seamless modality expansion [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
entry.summary: Researchers have developed Rosetta, a new multimodal pretraining framework designed to integrate new data modalities without losing previously learned knowledge. Rosetta uses a modular approach that preserves core knowledge in shared components while allowing modality-specific features to be added through plug-and-play modules. This design addresses the problem of catastrophic forgetting common in existing architectures like Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) and Mixture-of-Transformers (MoT). The framework introduces Momentum-Anchored Orthogonal Projection (MAOP), a technique that uses the optimizer's momentum to selectively block conflicting updates from new modalities while maintaining beneficial learning. Evaluations show that Rosetta maintains strong language and visual understanding, improves image generation, and enables effective cross-modal interactions. The researchers have made their code and models publicly available to support further advancements in multimodal AI.
